/kind bug

/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127797 changes the scheduler's event handler to use `assignedPod`/`unschedulablePod` EventResource, and `event.Match()` to handle those `assignedPod`/`unschedulablePod` EventResource correctly.

However, `AssignedPodUpdated` directly checks whether in-coming events are scale-down event or not without `event.Match()`. It directly uses `framework.Pod` event for a comparison, which always return `false` because now we're using `assignedPod`/`unschedulablePod`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

-->
Fixes #128195

Sorry for the trouble! I believe https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128223 should fix it.

By the way, why don't we run this alpha e2e test job in all PRs? 
Like this time, PRs which the author thinks are not related to the alpha features could break them actually.

> By the way, why don't we run this alpha e2e test job in all PRs? Like this time, PRs which the author thinks are not related to the alpha features could break them actually.

because is unstable and flaky, and impact developer workflow ... we want to have a very high bar in presubmits for required jobs, people developing alphas or experiment has to rely on optional and periodic jobs to not impact the rest of the project

we need to encourage the right behaviors on developers, owners of features must also maintain their own testing and jobs, if we make everyone responsible of the testing of all features, then no one is responsible and we get a flaky CI that will hide legit bugs... as part of graduation on features we have e2e and conformance test, so that is when those tests will be automatically run on presubmits, before that each feature owner should be accountable and responsible of their features included testing and reviewing the code and PRs that may intersect with their feature

> because is unstable and flaky

Then, that's the point, right? I do believe, regardless of whether the tests are for the alpha feature or not, we shouldn't have flaky tests. I don't think "this is the alpha feature" is an appropriate excuse that we can accept.

@AnishShah I was not aware this test was being removed, I put a lot of effort into this test. It is a **critical** E2E test that has ensured very good coverage and has assured quality for In-Place Pod Resize feature for a very long time. The feature **SHOULD NOT** make beta without this test.
